newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, seen steadying.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, seen steadying.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell on Monday on low turnover but traders said shares may receive a boost once the political situation becomes clearer.

"Today's turnover was low due to ongoing uncertainty on the market, but I expect things to become clearer by the end of the week and shares may begin rising then," Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A said.
The final official results from the general election held on November 10 show that the ruling Liberal Democrats have taken 25 seats in the 90-seat parliament.
But the rightist alliance of "Spring Parties" received a total of 45 seats.
Analysts said share prices may fall if the "Spring Parties" manage to form a government because of their protective stand towards Slovenia's joining the European Union.
The SBI index fell 0.86 percent or 10.06 points to 1,165.3. Overall nine shares fell, five rose and 10 were untraded.
Turnover crumbled to 78.4 million tolars from 193.6 million. Traders said turnover would likely remain low until the new government is formed.
"I wonder if there are any foreign investors left on our market at all," Apollonio said.
Drug producer Lek's A issue was the most actively traded, firming 1.98 percent or 370 tolars to close at 19,060 tolars on volume of 1,787 shares.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, tumbling 12.19 percent to 14,050 tolars on volume of 11 shares for total turnover of 161,550 tolars.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the day's biggest gainers, surging 6.61 percent to 12,580 tolars on volume of 45 shares for total turnover of 4.8 million tolars.
